Each seat in detail

Home Outfield Cheering Seats (Right)

ホーム外野応援指定席

¥2,700 – ¥4,500
What you see
Right-field stands, looking back at the whole diamond from behind the outfielders. You're far from the plate, but you're inside the noise.
Who sits here
The hardcore section. Everyone stands the entire game, sings a different song for every batter, and waves flags. Marines fans call themselves "the 26th player" and this is their home. Best place to feel what Japanese baseball actually is — worst place if you want to sit quietly and watch.

Home Outfield Cheering Seats (Left)

ホーム外野応援指定席(レフト)

¥2,600 – ¥4,500
What you see
Left-field stands. Outfielders play directly in front of you, and you can hear the right-field chanting across the park.
Who sits here
Marines fans who want the atmosphere without standing for nine innings. Families, couples, people with a beer. The compromise seat — cheap, lively, but you can stay in your chair.

Visitor Outfield Cheering Seats

ビジター外野応援指定席

¥3,000 – ¥5,000
What you see
Same as the home outfield, but on the other side.
Who sits here
Seibu Lions supporters, cheering against the home team. Only choose this if you want to root for Seibu — you'll be surrounded by their fans.

Infield C

内野指定席C

¥2,900 – ¥4,700
What you see
2nd floor, out toward the foul poles. High up and off to the side, but you're facing the field with a proper seat.
Who sits here
The cheapest actual seat in the house. Casual fans, families with kids, people arriving straight from work. Quiet, easy, no pressure to stand or sing.

Infield B / IB

内野指定席B / IB

¥4,800 – ¥5,900
What you see
2nd floor directly behind home plate. You see the entire field at once — the defensive shifts, where every ball is going, the whole shape of the game.
Who sits here
People who have watched a lot of baseball and pick this on purpose. Also the best seat for the fireworks and between-inning shows. Calm, focused, good value.

Infield A / IA

内野指定席A / IA

¥6,500 – ¥9,000
What you see
1st floor, between the infield and the outfield. Close enough to hear the ball, close enough to the outfield stands to hear the chanting.
Who sits here
The middle ground and the most mixed crowd — some cheering along with the outfield, some just watching. Good if you can't decide between atmosphere and a clean view.

Infield S / IS

内野指定席S / IS

¥8,600 – ¥14,200
What you see
1st floor right behind the dugouts, along the 1st and 3rd base lines. You can see players' faces and hear them talk. Armrests, cushions and cup holders.
Who sits here
Couples and small groups treating themselves, plus season-ticket regulars. Comfortable, close, and everyone is actually watching the game.

Field Wing Seats

フィールドウイング・シート

¥10,500
What you see
A deck that juts out over foul territory like a wing. The closest you get to the players at their eye level — you're basically on the field.
Who sits here
Fans who want the photos and the adrenaline. Small section, sells out fast. If you've never been to a Japanese ballpark, this is the one people remember.

Infield SS / VS

内野指定席SS / VS

¥13,000 – ¥15,000
What you see
Directly behind home plate on the lower level. You hear the ball hit the catcher's mitt and can actually judge a pitcher's breaking ball.
Who sits here
Serious fans, company guests, and people who came specifically to watch the pitching. The most expensive general seats, with the widest chairs and cushioned backs.

Two novelty seats, if you want a story

Submarine Seat (1st base side) LOTTE 雪見だいふく サブマリン・シート

¥15,500

A sponsor-branded box down near field level. Novelty seat — comes with the LOTTE branding and a very close view.

Players' Seat プレイヤーズ・シート

¥9,500

Themed seating tied to individual players. Fun if you already have a favourite on the roster.

Things worth knowing

  • Prices move. Chiba Lotte uses dynamic pricing, so every price here is what it costs today and can change before you buy.
  • Infield GⅠ (backstop premium) and Panorama Counter Seats are already sold out for this game.
  • Tickets are QR codes. Whoever buys them can send the ticket to your phone by email or LINE — you don't need an account, an app, or the buyer to be with you at the gate.
  • One ticket per person, including children who need their own seat. Under 4 gets in free if they sit on a lap.
  • It gets windy. ZOZO Marine is right on Tokyo Bay and the sea wind picks up after dark, even in September. Bring a layer for a night game.
  • Getting there: Kaihimmakuhari Station (JR Keiyo Line), then about 15 minutes on foot or a short bus ride.
